title: Month 18
subtitle: The eighteen-month visit is this month. It is the one with the autism screen, and it is a conversation, not a verdict.

baby.development: Your child is running, may be climbing stairs with a hand held, and says around ten to twenty words. They can point to three or more body parts and are starting to pretend, like feeding a doll.

you.body: If you are pregnant again, eighteen months is the age gap that is hardest on the body. Ask for help with the lifting.
you.mind: The autism screen is a questionnaire, not a diagnosis. A positive screen means a closer look, and a closer look early is the thing that helps.

coreActions.title: Go to the eighteen-month visit
coreActions.why: This is the autism screen, the next vaccine set, and the language check, and it is the visit where a concern is easiest to raise.
coreActions.detail: The US schedule at eighteen months is DTaP and hepatitis A, with others depending on what was given earlier. The screen is usually the M-CHAT, eighteen questions. Answer them about what the child does, not what you hope they do. A referral for an evaluation is not a diagnosis.

coreActions.title: Name everything, all day
coreActions.why: Vocabulary at this age grows from hearing words attached to things that are happening.
coreActions.detail: Narrate what you are doing and what the child is doing. Expand what they say: if they say dog, say yes, a big brown dog. Read the same books. Sing the same songs. Screen time does not do this.

coreActions.title: Decide your limits before the tantrum
coreActions.why: A limit that changes depending on how loud the child is teaches that loud works.
coreActions.detail: Pick the few things that are non-negotiable and hold them every time. Everything else can be a choice between two options, which is what a toddler actually wants. Say the limit once, calmly, and then stop talking.

alsoKnow.title: Pretend play starts now
alsoKnow.body: Feeding a doll, stirring a pot, and putting a toy to bed are the beginnings of pretend play, and they are a language and social milestone.

alsoKnow.title: Stairs need a gate until three
alsoKnow.body: A child can climb stairs with a hand held at eighteen months but cannot be trusted on them alone until around three. Gate the top and the bottom.

redFlags.text: Choking — cannot breathe, cough, or make a sound
A fever over 100.4°F with unusual sleepiness or a rash
Feeling hopeless, or thoughts of harming yourself or the child
